about: Free resources for people experiencing homelessness in Portland, OR. Public domain (CC0). Verify every change before committing: see CONTRIBUTING.md.

resources.name: Operation Nightwatch
resources.desc: A warm place to be in the evening, when other agencies are closed: coffee, a meal, supplies, company, and mental health services.
resources.detail: At St. Stephen's Episcopal Church. Everyone is welcome just as they are; no faith practice required. Agape Village runs an overnight shelter in the same building (see Agape Village Overnight Shelters).

resources.name: Street Roots
resources.desc: Sell newspapers for $1 (buy for $0.25). Keep ALL profit and tips. Set your own hours. Bring a pet. 800+ vendors.
resources.detail: Fastest path to income. Start earning within days of orientation.
resources.hoursText: Office: Mon, Thu, Sat 8:30am-noon; Wed 8am-2pm; Fri 8:30am-2pm. New vendor orientation Wed & Fri at 2:15pm.

resources.name: GLITTER
resources.desc: $21.25/hour pick-up shifts collecting litter and camp waste, on foot or bike. No background check. Fill out a W-9 tax form.
resources.detail: Shifts chosen by lottery, not guaranteed. Mon 9am: Gateway or SE Holgate MAX stop. Tue 9am: SE Holgate or Parkrose MAX stop. Wed 8:30am at Couch St: members only. Thu 8:30am at Couch St: non-members. Won national award Jul 2026.
resources.highlight: NO ID NEEDED. New? Go Thursday, arrive from 8am.
resources.hoursText: New workers: Thursday 8:30am at 624 NW Couch St (arrive from 8am)

resources.name: Voz Workers' Center
resources.desc: Same-day paid work: landscaping, moving, construction, cleaning. $22/hr minimum guaranteed. All pay goes directly to you.
resources.detail: Nonprofit worker center. ESL classes, safety training, workforce development. New member orientations twice a month.

resources.name: Clean Start
resources.desc: Paid 9-month trainee program. Sidewalk cleaning, graffiti removal. 40 hrs/wk. Peer mentoring plus housing, healthcare, and recovery services.
resources.detail: Above minimum wage. Full-time roles are union with benefits. 130+ employees. Majority exit with long-term housing and permanent job.

resources.name: Central City Staffing
resources.desc: 12-month on-call trainee program. Work across 47+ CCC buildings. Janitorial, maintenance, front desk. Flexible scheduling.
resources.detail: Low-barrier. Accommodates treatment and appointments. Over 40% of CCC staff are former clients. Applications open 1st Monday of each month.
resources.hoursText: Email: CCStaffing@ccconcern.org. Apps open 1st Monday monthly.

resources.name: PeopleReady
resources.desc: Temporary shifts in construction, warehouse, hospitality, manufacturing, retail. Pick shifts on the JobStack app.
resources.detail: No resume required. Set your own schedule. W-2 paid employment. Need valid I-9 identification. Branch: 204 N Killingsworth St.
resources.hoursText: Branch Mon-Fri 9am-6pm. Or pick shifts on the JobStack app.

resources.name: Cultivate Initiatives
resources.desc: Paid internship: 9 days of work over 3 weeks. Beautification and cleanup work. Path to full-time employment with benefits, PTO, and 401(k).
resources.detail: Call for current pay and next orientation. Workforce Hub also has showers and laundry. Call to check if you can use them without joining the program.
resources.highlight: Paid internship leads to full-time job with benefits

resources.name: RRBC (Rapid Response Bio-Clean)
resources.desc: Campsite cleanup and biohazard remediation. Training in safety, de-escalation, CPR, and Naloxone.
resources.detail: Hires people with lived experience of homelessness and criminal history. City of Portland contractor.
resources.hoursText: Apply online at rrbc-inc.com or email contact@rrbc-inc.com

resources.name: Employment Access Center
resources.desc: Career mapping, resume help, interview prep, job leads. Employer presentations every Wednesday 10-11am. Free computers, copiers, fax, phone.
resources.detail: Placed 551 people in jobs in 2024. Ask any CCC case manager for referral.
resources.hoursText: Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm, by referral. CCC clients: ask your case manager. Others: call (503) 226-7387.

resources.name: Blackburn Center
resources.desc: Employment specialists plus transportation assistance to get to work. Resume help, career exploration, mock interviews.
resources.detail: Healthcare, recovery, housing, and employment all under one roof. Great for East Portland residents.

resources.name: Constructing Hope
resources.desc: FREE 10-week construction training. Carpentry, electrical, plumbing. Resume help, interview prep, boots and tools provided. 3 years of post-grad support.
resources.detail: Average starting wage $21/hr. 1,300+ graduates placed. Accepts people with criminal history (63% of participants). Need state ID and GED/diploma.
resources.hoursText: Info session in person every Monday at 1pm (not holidays). Bring ID and diploma or GED. Classes start Jan, Apr, Jun, Sep.

resources.name: POIC Portland
resources.desc: Multiple paid training tracks: healthcare certifications, semiconductor/tech (Microchip partnership), outdoor conservation.
resources.detail: Paid internships available. Free or low-cost industry-recognized certifications. Youth and adult programs.

resources.name: Oregon Tradeswomen
resources.desc: Free skilled trades training for women and gender-diverse people. Construction, electrical, welding. Leads to union apprenticeships with full benefits.
resources.detail: Funded through Worksystems and Future Ready Oregon. Union apprenticeship means career path plus full benefits.
resources.highlight: Next cohort starting soon. Check website.
resources.addr: 16790 NE Mason St, Suite 100, Portland, OR 97230
resources.hoursText: Office Mon-Thu 9am-4pm; other days by appointment. Request an info session on the website.

resources.name: Portland Youth Builders
resources.desc: GED completion plus construction pre-apprenticeship. Combined education and career training for young adults.
resources.detail: 2026-2027 classes active. For younger guests needing both education credentials and a career path into the trades.
resources.hoursText: Call (503) 286-9350 or email to get started. New classes start every couple of months.

resources.name: Bridges to Change
resources.desc: Peer Wellness Specialist certification, a paid career pathway into behavioral health work. Also runs Club Hope, a drop-in recovery center in Gresham with showers, laundry, and food.
resources.detail: Turn your lived experience into a career helping others. Growing field with strong demand.
resources.hoursText: Check bridgestochange.com for Club Hope hours

resources.name: WorkSource Portland Metro
resources.desc: Free resume workshops, interview prep, job leads, training scholarships. Veterans get priority services. Register in iMatchSkills.
resources.detail: Part of the American Job Center network. Workshops on soft skills, Excel, Word, computer basics, and state jobs. All services free. Centers: 30 N Webster St, Suite E, (503) 280-6046; 6401 SE Foster Rd, (503) 934-0630; 18633 SE Stark St, Suite 201, Gresham, (503) 669-7112.
resources.hoursText: Walk in without an appointment, or call a center. Closed Nov 26-27, 2026.

resources.name: SE Works / WorkSource SE
resources.desc: Full career center plus NewStart Reentry Resource Center for people with criminal history. CDL training, career mapping.
resources.detail: Reentry services at 8044 SE Harold St. Road-to-success curriculum, career mapping, resume help, WIOA-funded services.

resources.name: Goodwill Job Connection
resources.desc: Job placement assistance and multi-employer job fairs. Goodwill also hires directly and provides vocational opportunities.
resources.detail: Mission: vocational opportunities for people with disabilities and barriers to employment. Job fairs 3rd Tuesday monthly. Also Powell (9015 SE Powell Blvd) Mon-Fri 9am-5:30pm, Airport Outlet (5950 NE 122nd Ave) Mon-Fri 9am-5:30pm, Halsey (12250 NE Halsey) Mon, Wed, Fri 9am-5:30pm.
resources.hoursText: Portland Job Connection (1943 SE 6th Ave) Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm

resources.name: PDX ID Assistance
resources.desc: Free drop-in clinics to replace birth certificates (all 50 states), driver's licenses, and ID cards. Paul Susi pays the fees himself.
resources.detail: Without an ID, most employment programs are out of reach. Get your ID first, everything else gets easier.
resources.highlight: Paused as of Nov 3, 2026. Check the website for new dates.
resources.hoursText: Paused. New dates and locations will be posted on the website.

resources.name: Oregon Free ID Card
resources.desc: Oregon law waives the $44.50 state ID card fee for people experiencing homelessness. Get a Declaration of Homelessness form first.
resources.detail: Go to Transition Projects (650 NW Irving St) to get the Declaration form, then take it to the DMV.
resources.hoursText: Get form from Transition Projects, then visit any DMV

resources.name: Oregon Lifeline
resources.desc: Free wireless phone service through Access Wireless if you receive Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or SSI. One phone per household.

resources.name: Social Security Card
resources.desc: Call SSA to request a replacement Social Security card. You need your SSN for most employment.
resources.detail: Portland offices, Mon-Fri 9am-4pm: 1538 SW Yamhill St and 17925 SE Division St. Make an appointment to skip the line.

resources.name: Free Oregon Birth Certificate
resources.desc: If you were born in Oregon and are homeless, you can get your own birth certificate free through a participating service provider.
resources.detail: The provider helps with the form, pays the fee, and gives an address to mail it to. Ask a shelter or day center if they take part, or see the provider map on the state's page.

resources.name: Blanchet House
resources.desc: Meals 3 times daily, 6 days a week. Bethanie's Room overnight shelter for women and nonbinary guests. Clothing distributed Mon-Sat.
resources.detail: Drop-in daily 6am-10pm. Ask about the transitional housing program. Blanchet Farm in Carlton for longer-term recovery.
resources.hoursText: Mon-Sat 6am-10pm. Meals served at set times.

resources.name: Union Gospel Mission
resources.desc: 200,000+ meals per year. Clothing, hygiene, showers. 100-bed shelter nightly. Search and Rescue van visits camps 5 nights per week.
resources.detail: FREE legal services for criminal record expungement. Mobile showers: Wed 9am-12:30pm at the mission; Mon 10am-1:30pm at 1302 SE Ankeny St; Sat 11am-2pm at 9715 SE Powell Blvd. Clothing Wed-Fri 4pm.
resources.hoursText: To-go meals Wed-Fri 2pm & 8pm, Sat 11am. Showers Wed 9am-12:30pm here. No meals Sun-Tue.

resources.name: Potluck in the Park
resources.desc: Free hot meal every Sunday, rain or shine, 52 weeks a year since 1991. No questions asked.
resources.detail: North Park Blocks, beside the sculpture on NW Glisan St between 8th Ave and Park Ave. A Portland institution for over 30 years. Everyone welcome.
resources.addr: NW Park Ave & NW Glisan St, Portland, OR

resources.name: Night Strike
resources.sub: CityTeam: Thursday night meal, haircuts, foot care
resources.desc: A hot meal on Thursday nights, plus haircuts, foot washing, and replacement clothing and sleeping bags.
resources.detail: First come, first served. Now indoors at Liberation Street Church. The schedule changes on Thanksgiving and from mid-December to early January; check the website.

resources.name: Rahab's Sisters
resources.sub: Friday dinner and weekday drop-in for women, trans, and nonbinary people
resources.desc: A restaurant-style Friday dinner with clothing and hygiene supplies, and a Wednesday and Thursday drop-in with lunch.
resources.detail: Open to all women, trans, and nonbinary people. Thursdays include medical care. Help with benefits and ID: ask at a Friday gathering. Check the monthly calendar on the website for changes.

resources.name: St. André Bessette Church Hospitality
resources.sub: Formerly Downtown Chapel: sack lunch and Friday dinner
resources.desc: A morning sack lunch Tuesday to Thursday, afternoon hospitality, and a hot Friday evening meal, with some clothing and hygiene supplies.
resources.detail: Ages 18+. First come, first served. Hours are from 211info; call to confirm.
resources.hoursText: Tue-Thu sack lunch 9:30-10:30am, hospitality 1-4pm. Fri hot meal 6:30-7:30pm.

resources.name: First Baptist Drop-In
resources.sub: Hot meal Monday and Thursday downtown
resources.desc: A hot meal twice a week for people who are homeless or low-income, plus groceries, clothing, and toiletries while they last.
resources.detail: Next to the Central Library, at 11th and Taylor.

resources.name: Grace Memorial Community Dinner
resources.desc: A free sit-down dinner every Sunday evening. All are welcome.

resources.name: All Saints Woodstock Hot Meals
resources.desc: A hot lunch every Saturday, to eat there or take out. The church also runs the Woodstock Pantry.
resources.detail: Hours are from 211info; call to confirm.

resources.name: Highland Christian Center
resources.desc: A community breakfast every Sunday morning, and a food pantry twice a month.
resources.detail: Pantry needs proof of address: 1st and 3rd Friday 9-11am in Nov-Dec, 2nd and 4th Friday Jan-Oct. Hours are from 211info.

resources.name: Clackamas Service Center
resources.desc: Sit-down or to-go meals four days a week, a walk-up grocery pantry, free showers, and clothing.
resources.detail: Walk-up pantry Tue & Thu from 11:45am: give first name, last initial, ZIP, and household size; the list fills fast. Showers and clothing Tue-Thu 10am-1pm (15-minute limit; arrive before noon). Mail service available.

resources.name: PDX Saints Love Day Center
resources.desc: Warm meals, showers and laundry, clothing, hygiene kits, phone charging, a place to rest, and peer support.
resources.detail: Low barrier. Help with ID and birth records, OHP and SNAP forms, housing, and detox or treatment referrals. Haircuts Mondays 10am-2pm. The mobile clinic visits here; see its card for dates.

resources.name: Recovery Café Roseway
resources.desc: A recovery community with a free lunch, espresso bar, recovery circles, and peer support.
resources.detail: Visit as a guest first. Members stay drug- and alcohol-free in the space and join a weekly Recovery Circle. Lunch about 12:15-1:30pm.

resources.name: Catholic Charities Women's Day Services
resources.desc: A weekday drop-in with lunch, coffee, showers, laundry, phone and voicemail, a mailing address, and computers.
resources.detail: For women 25 and older experiencing homelessness who are not parenting. Well-behaved pets allowed. Hours are from 211info; call to confirm.
resources.addr: 2740 SE Powell Blvd, Suite 5, Portland, OR 97202

resources.name: HIV Day Center
resources.desc: Hot breakfast and lunch on weekdays, plus phone and mail service, computers, showers, laundry, and clothing.
resources.detail: For low-income people living with HIV/AIDS. Self-referral welcome.

resources.name: My Brothers and Sisters Kitchen
resources.desc: A weekly community lunch for individuals and families experiencing homelessness, at St. Henry Catholic Church.
resources.detail: Not held in July or August. Hours are from 211info.

resources.name: Zarephath Kitchen & Pantry
resources.sub: Gresham hot lunch and grocery pantry
resources.desc: A hot lunch Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, and a grocery pantry with staples, meat, produce, and dairy.
resources.detail: Enter through the church parking lot off Ava Ave, or from Eastman Pkwy north of Powell. Thanksgiving week: lunch Mon, Thanksgiving dinner Wed 11am-1pm; pantry Tue Nov 24 3-5pm and Wed Nov 25 10am-12:30pm; no pantry Thu or Fri.
resources.hoursText: Lunch Mon, Wed, Fri 11am-1pm. Pantry Thu 10am-12:30pm.

resources.name: Sunshine Division Free Food Markets
resources.sub: Free groceries, NW and SE Portland
resources.desc: Free groceries you choose yourself, like a store, at two markets.
resources.detail: By appointment on the website or by phone. Bring photo ID if you have one; no one is turned away without it. SE market: 12436 SE Stark St, Mon-Fri 9am-noon and 1-4pm, 971-325-8810.
resources.hoursText: By appointment. NW: Tue, Wed, Fri 9am-noon & 1-4pm; Thu 11am-3pm & 4-7pm; Sat 9am-2pm.

resources.name: Lift UP Preston's Pantry
resources.desc: A shopping-style pantry with meat, eggs, produce, dairy, and dry goods, up to twice a month.
resources.detail: No ID or proof of income needed, but income must meet guidelines. Thu and Fri shopping order is by lottery; arrive no earlier than 2pm. Enter at the rear of First United Methodist Church, by the playground.

resources.name: Francis Center
resources.desc: Free food, plus clothing, hygiene items, and blankets when available. No appointment or documents needed.
resources.detail: Unhoused guests can come once a week. Bring bags.

resources.name: SnowCap Community Services
resources.desc: Food every weekday plus some evenings, up to twice a month.
resources.detail: New clients apply online or call. Food is handed out outside: dress for the weather and bring bags. Behind The Rockwood Center; use the west driveway off Stark. The mobile clinic visits here; see its card.

resources.name: Salvation Army Food Pantries
resources.desc: Food boxes at two Salvation Army centers. Proof of address is not needed if you are homeless.
resources.detail: N Williams (5325 N Williams Ave): Wed & Fri 9am-1pm, one box a week. Gresham Corps (473 SE 194th Ave): Mon-Thu 9am-noon, one box every 30 days. Each serves certain ZIP codes.
resources.hoursText: N Williams Wed & Fri 9am-1pm; Gresham Mon-Thu 9am-noon

resources.name: Northeast Emergency Food Program
resources.desc: Fruit, vegetables, bread, meat, and dairy, shopping style, weekly.
resources.detail: Arrive within 30 minutes of opening to get a number. In the basement of the Luther Memorial building.

resources.name: Mainspring
resources.sub: Food bags and clothing pantry, NE 82nd
resources.desc: Pre-made food bags once a week, and a clothing and hygiene pantry every 14 days.
resources.detail: Low barrier. Bring bags. Closed on holidays and when Portland Public Schools close for weather.
resources.hoursText: Food bags Thu 9am-1pm; clothing Tue & Thu 10am-1pm. Closed Nov 22-28.

resources.name: Clay Street Table Pantry
resources.desc: A shopping-style grocery pantry open to everyone in need of food.
resources.hoursText: 4th Thursday of the month, 11am-noon. November falls on Thanksgiving: call first.

resources.name: Oregon Food Bank FoodFinder
resources.sub: Map of every free food site near you
resources.desc: A searchable map of food pantries, free meals, and other free food in your neighborhood, including small church pantries not listed here.

resources.name: St. Michael's Catholic Church
resources.desc: Hot lunch plus pre-packaged snacks, new socks, gloves, and hand warmers. Prayer and conversation.
resources.detail: Served under the west side of the Hawthorne Bridge, not at the church. No signup needed.
resources.addr: Hawthorne Bridge west end, SW Naito Pkwy, Portland, OR

resources.name: William Temple House
resources.desc: Food pantry where you choose your own groceries: staples, produce, meat, dairy. Resource navigation by appointment. Thrift store on site.
resources.detail: Book at williamtemple.simplybook.me or at the front desk. A few walk-in slots each pantry day; same-day wait can be 20 minutes to 2 hours. Twice a month per household. Pantry is in the basement; the side door off the parking lot avoids stairs.
resources.hoursText: Pantry Wed 9:30am-12:30pm, Thu 1-4pm, by appointment (some walk-in slots). Closed MLK Day, Juneteenth, July 4, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day.

resources.name: Transition Projects
resources.desc: Shelter plus employment navigation plus mail receipt services. Declaration of Homelessness forms for free DMV ID.
resources.detail: Showers and laundry Mon-Fri 9am-noon (last shower 11:30, last laundry 11:00). Free haircuts Wed-Fri noon-2pm. Clothing closet Mon, Wed, Fri 1:30-2:30pm. Lockers daily. Staff can sign the form for a free Oregon ID.
resources.hoursText: Resource Center Mon-Fri 8:30am-3:30pm. Mail Mon-Fri 8:30-10:30am and 12:30-3:30pm. Shelter referrals Mon-Fri 8:30-9:30am.

resources.name: Portland Rescue Mission
resources.desc: Shelter, meals, mail services, addiction recovery programs. Crisis care and resource referrals since 1949.
resources.detail: Burnside Shelter offers free, 24/7 drop-in emergency services, including restrooms and two meals a day. Overnight shelter is for men.
resources.hoursText: Burnside Shelter drop-in: open 24/7. Two meals a day; ask for meal times.

resources.name: JOIN
resources.desc: Housing navigation, showers, food, and day center. Outreach teams meet you where you are. Direct pathway from streets to housing.
resources.detail: Day Space for people experiencing homelessness. Housing services are not accessed through walk-ins at the Day Space; ask about referrals.
resources.hoursText: Day Space: Mon, Wed, Fri 9am-5pm; Tue, Thu 10am-4pm; Sat-Sun 9am-5pm

resources.name: CityTeam Portland
resources.desc: Rehabilitation, shelter, food. Women's showers Mon/Wed/Fri 1-3pm. 100-bed overnight shelter 9pm-6:30am nightly. Pets welcome (leashed or crated).

resources.name: NW Pilot Project
resources.desc: Housing navigation and rent/deposit assistance focused on older adults 55+ experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
resources.detail: If you're 55+ and homeless, this is your first call. They focus exclusively on older adult housing.
resources.hoursText: Office: Mon-Wed 9am-noon and 1-4pm; Thu 1-4pm; Fri by appointment only

resources.name: Salvation Army Portland
resources.desc: Two first-come, first-served overnight shelters: Burnside Shelter (30 SW 2nd Ave) for women, and Moore Street Shelter (5325 N Williams Ave) for adult women and men.
resources.detail: Burnside: 8pm-8am nightly, (503) 227-0810. Moore Street: 8pm-6am nightly, (971) 230-5313. The City warns that budget cuts may change City-funded shelters; City Shelter Services: (503) 823-1340.
resources.hoursText: Nightly from 8pm. Burnside until 8am, Moore Street until 6am.

resources.name: SE Grand Recovery Shelter
resources.desc: City-funded overnight shelter for adults who want an alcohol- and drug-free place to sleep.
resources.detail: Arrive sober. Your bed from last night is held for tonight; new people get the beds that are left. Don't line up more than 30 minutes before 9pm.
resources.hoursText: Nightly 9pm-7am. New people get leftover beds.

resources.name: City of Portland Shelter Services
resources.sub: Find a City shelter bed, or ask for outreach
resources.desc: The City runs overnight shelters and 24/7 pod and tiny-home villages. A live map shows which overnight shelters have beds tonight.
resources.detail: Check the shelter availability map on portland.gov/shelter-services. Pod and tiny-home villages only take referrals from outreach workers: call 311 to ask for one. The City is closing and combining some shelters because of budget cuts, and a City workers’ strike that began Nov 9 may slow 311.

resources.name: Bybee Lakes Hope Center
resources.sub: Helping Hands Reentry: 24/7 shelter, North Portland
resources.desc: A large 24/7 shelter for men, women, and families, with up to 30 days of emergency shelter and a longer reentry program.
resources.detail: By referral. Call the center to ask about open beds and how to get a referral. You must commit to sobriety. The mobile clinic visits here; see its card for dates.
resources.addr: 14355 N Bybee Lake Ct, Portland, OR 97203
resources.hoursText: Open 24/7 by referral. Call to ask about beds.

resources.name: Severe Weather Shelters
resources.sub: Multnomah County: open only in dangerous cold or heat
resources.desc: Extra overnight shelters the County opens on top of year-round beds when the weather is dangerous.
resources.detail: Check multco.us/care-when-its-cold, or call 211, to find out if they are open tonight. 211 may stay open longer during weather emergencies. Libraries and the Behavioral Health Resource Center are warm daytime spaces.
resources.hoursText: Only during weather emergencies. Check daily in cold weather.

resources.name: 211info
resources.sub: Help line for shelter and services
resources.desc: Free help line that connects you to shelter, family shelter, warming centers, food, and other services.
resources.detail: Families looking for shelter call 211 to be screened. If 211 won’t dial from your phone, call 866-698-6155. Text your zip code to 898211 (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm). Interpreters available. Longer hours during emergencies.

resources.name: Janus Youth Access Center
resources.sub: Ages 16-24: the way in to youth shelter and drop-ins
resources.desc: Young people 16-24 who are homeless start here to get screened for youth shelter, drop-in centers, and housing.
resources.detail: Call to talk with a screener, or leave your name and a callback number. After 5pm, go to Porch Light shelter at 8:45pm.
resources.hoursText: Screenings 9am-5pm, every day of the year

resources.name: Porch Light Youth Shelter
resources.desc: Nightly shelter for youth 16-24 with meals, bunk beds, and showers. LGBTQ affirming.
resources.detail: Come to the door any time between 9pm and 5am; beds are first come, first served. An intake worker meets with you in the morning.

resources.name: New Avenues for Youth Drop-In
resources.desc: Daytime drop-in with meals six days a week, showers, laundry, clothes, computers, and advocates for jobs, school, and housing.
resources.detail: Get screened first through the Janus Youth Access Center (503-432-3986). Meals are served in the first hour of each session. East County drop-in: 470 SE 165th Ave, Mon-Fri 10am-6pm.

resources.name: Outside In Youth Services
resources.desc: Meals, a health clinic, counseling, school and job help, and housing connections for young people.
resources.detail: For ages 16-24 screened into youth services. You can start the screening here, or call the Janus Youth Access Center at 503-432-3986.
resources.hoursText: Come in or call to start screening

resources.name: p:ear
resources.sub: Drop-in for homeless youth: food, art, mentoring
resources.desc: A drop-in for young people experiencing homelessness with food, mentoring, art and education programs, and mail pickup.

resources.name: Call to Safety
resources.desc: Free, confidential 24/7 support for survivors of domestic and sexual violence: safety planning and help finding DV shelter.
resources.detail: Interpreters available. Its website shows each day which DV shelters are taking new people.

resources.name: Raphael House
resources.desc: Emergency shelter and support for domestic violence survivors and their children.
resources.detail: Check calltosafety.org to see if Raphael House is taking new people, then call with a completed Safety and Stabilization Assessment (SSA). The Gateway Center can help you do the SSA.

resources.name: Bradley Angle
resources.desc: Emergency shelter and housing help for anyone affected by domestic violence, with programs for Black and LGBTQIA+ survivors.
resources.detail: Call the intake line or use the request form on the website. For crisis help any time, call Call to Safety at 503-235-5333.

resources.name: Gateway Center
resources.sub: Multnomah County: help for abuse survivors
resources.desc: Safety planning, restraining orders, and connections to DV shelter for survivors of partner abuse, sexual assault, and trafficking.
resources.detail: Waits can be long and it sometimes fills for the day, so call first. Calls are returned from a blocked number. After hours, call Call to Safety at 503-235-5333.

resources.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
resources.desc: Safe, confidential, anonymous help for American Indians and Alaska Natives affected by domestic, dating, or sexual violence.
resources.detail: Call or text 1-844-762-8483, or chat on the website.

resources.name: Agape Village Shelter at St. Stephen's
resources.desc: Overnight shelter for adults in the same building as Operation Nightwatch: a safe night of sleep. Pets welcome if on a leash or in a crate.
resources.detail: Open 9pm-7am; arrive no earlier than 8:30pm, doors close 11pm. Phone answered 8-11pm only, no voicemail. Once you arrive, if you leave you can't come back until the next night. Last night's guests get in first, then recent guests, then first-timers in order of arrival. Your photo is taken for a badge at check-in. No showers, no drug use, no weapons. Agape's second shelter is at Central Nazarene, 9715 SE Powell Blvd.
resources.hoursText: Doors 9pm-11pm. Nights not posted, so call 8-11pm to check.

resources.name: Agape Village Shelter at Central Nazarene
resources.sub: Adults only, overnight, first come first served
resources.desc: City-funded overnight shelter for adults in a church in outer SE Portland. Pets welcome if on a leash or in a crate.
resources.detail: Line up no earlier than 8:30pm. Open 9pm-6:30am; doors close 11pm. Phone answered 8-11pm only, no voicemail. Once you arrive, if you leave you can't come back until the next night. Your photo is taken for a badge at check-in. No showers, no drug use, no weapons.

resources.name: Behavioral Health Resource Center
resources.desc: Drop-in day center with shower, laundry, shelter, and bridge housing. Mental health and substance use support.
resources.detail: Multnomah County run. Bridge housing while you stabilize. No appointment needed for day center.
resources.hoursText: Day center open daily 8am-8pm. Closed 11am-3pm on the 4th Friday of each month.

resources.name: Rose Haven
resources.desc: Clothing, supplies, meals, showers, laundry, and case management for women, children, and gender-diverse people.
resources.detail: Showers and laundry are for registered guests. Sign up during service hours. Showers first come, first served.

resources.name: Old Town Clinic
resources.desc: Primary care doctor visits and an on-site pharmacy in Old Town. Visits in person, by phone, or by video.
resources.detail: Sliding-fee scale. Takes OHP, Medicare, and self-pay. They don't turn anyone away for lack of insurance or inability to pay. Call to schedule.
resources.hoursText: By appointment. Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 8am-5pm; Wed 9am-5pm.

resources.name: Hooper Detox
resources.desc: Medically supported withdrawal from alcohol, opioids, and other drugs. Walk in by 7:30am, Monday to Friday, for morning triage.
resources.detail: Admission depends on need and open beds, not first come, first served. If you aren't admitted, ask about a standby spot or an afternoon admission. Outpatient help Mon-Fri 1-4pm, walk-in or by appointment. Bring a state ID or driver's license, and your insurance card if you have one.
resources.highlight: Walk in by 7:30am, Monday to Friday
resources.hoursText: Admission triage Mon-Fri 6:45-7:45am. Outpatient Mon-Fri 1-4pm. Closed July 4, Thanksgiving, and Christmas.

resources.name: Fora Health Detox
resources.desc: Medically supported detox from alcohol and drugs. Walk in by 7:30am any day of the week.
resources.detail: Admission depends on beds and a medical check. Weekends: OHP only. Private insurance or outside Multnomah, Washington, or Clackamas County: call first, Mon-Fri 7:30am-4:30pm. No one is denied for inability to pay. Medications for addiction: walk in Mon-Fri 9am-4pm or call 503-713-9156.
resources.addr: 10230 SE Cherry Blossom Dr, Portland, OR 97216
resources.hoursText: Detox: arrive by 7:30am, every day. Addiction medication walk-in Mon-Fri 9am-4pm.

resources.name: Old Town Recovery Center
resources.sub: Central City Concern: walk-in addiction and mental health care
resources.desc: Outpatient mental health care and addiction treatment, including Suboxone, counseling, peer support, and an on-site pharmacy.
resources.detail: Walk in or call to start care. Takes OHP and self-pay; no one turned away for inability to pay.

resources.name: CODA Portland Recovery Center
resources.desc: Medication treatment for opioid use disorder, including methadone.
resources.detail: Call for a short phone screening; most people get an appointment the same or next day. Sliding scale if you have no insurance. Buses 12, 19, 20, 70.

resources.name: Alcohol & Drug Helpline
resources.sub: Lines for Life: 24/7 substance use help
resources.desc: Free, confidential support and treatment referrals for people using alcohol or drugs, and for their families.
resources.detail: Interpreters available. Search treatment that takes OHP at treatmentaccessline.org.

resources.name: Portland AA
resources.desc: Free AA meetings all over Portland, every day, including Spanish and ASL meetings. No sign-up.
resources.detail: Find a meeting at pdxaa.org/meetings or in the Meeting Guide app.

resources.name: Portland NA
resources.desc: Free Narcotics Anonymous meetings around Portland. No sign-up.

resources.name: Alano Club of Portland
resources.sub: Recovery center with 100+ meetings a week
resources.desc: A recovery community center hosting over 100 free recovery meetings a week, plus classes.
resources.detail: Open to anyone in or seeking recovery. Meeting schedule on the website.
resources.hoursText: Office open daily 11am-7pm; meetings at many times

resources.name: The Miracles Club
resources.desc: Free peer recovery mentors, meetings, and help connecting to housing, treatment, jobs, and health care.
resources.detail: Call or apply for services on the website. Second site: Miracles Central, 1306 NE 2nd Ave.
resources.addr: 4200 NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Portland, OR 97211

resources.name: 4D Recovery
resources.desc: Young people in or seeking recovery get peer mentors, help with housing, jobs, and OHP, and nightly meetings and sober events.
resources.addr: 11010 SE Division St, Suite 200, Portland, OR 97266
resources.hoursText: Call or use the referral form on the website

resources.name: The Peer Company
resources.desc: Free peer support from people with lived experience of mental health or addiction: help getting into detox, treatment, and housing.
resources.detail: Self-refer with the form on mhaoforegon.org, or call.

resources.name: NAYA
resources.sub: Native American Youth and Family Center
resources.desc: Native-led center with a food pantry, clothing closet, rent and utility help, family shelter, youth housing and recovery support, and job programs.
resources.detail: For Native American people and families, from infants to Elders. Call first.

resources.name: NARA Indian Health Clinic
resources.desc: Family medicine, mental health, HIV/STI and hepatitis C testing, and addiction treatment for Native American and Alaska Native people.
resources.detail: Call for an appointment. Sliding-scale fees. Bring a tribal or Native ID if you have one. Also: NARA Wellness Center, 12360 E Burnside St, 971-279-4800.

resources.name: Painted Horse Recovery
resources.desc: Drop-in recovery support with Wellbriety and Native-based AA and NA meetings, skill groups, and culture nights. Open to anyone seeking recovery.

resources.name: Outside In Medical Clinic
resources.desc: Primary care, an on-site pharmacy, and medication to treat addiction, for ages 13 and up.
resources.detail: Stop by or call to ask about a same-day visit; spots depend on the day. No one is turned away for inability to pay; most insurance accepted. Ages 15-17 can come without a guardian. Second clinic at 16144 E Burnside St: Mon-Wed 8:30am-5pm, Thu-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm, closed 12-12:45pm.
resources.hoursText: Downtown: Mon, Thu, Fri 8:30am-5pm; Tue, Wed 8:30am-7pm (2nd Tuesday of the month from 10am). Same-day visits when available.

resources.name: Outside In Drug User Health Services
resources.desc: Free naloxone (Narcan) and overdose-prevention training, HIV, hepatitis C, and syphilis testing, and drug checking.
resources.detail: For adults 18 and up. Free.

resources.name: Multnomah County Mobile Clinic
resources.desc: A medical van that visits sites around the county: illness and injuries, exams, vaccines, pregnancy tests, limited prescriptions, and dental cleanings at some stops.
resources.detail: Walk-ins welcome while spots last, seen in order of arrival. Pay what you can; if you can't pay, you can still get care. Some stops are at shelters or women's centers that may only serve their own guests: text or call 971-940-3149 during clinic hours to check before you go, and to ask about wait times.
resources.highlight: Walk-ins welcome. Pay what you can.

stops.addr: 14355 N Bybee Lake Ct, Portland, OR 97203

stops.place: Portland Community College SE Campus (dental cleanings too)
Behavioral Health Resource Center (dental cleanings too)

stops.addr: 1431 SE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Portland, OR 97214
14355 N Bybee Lake Ct, Portland, OR 97203

stops.place: Behavioral Health Resource Center (dental cleanings too)

stops.addr: 14355 N Bybee Lake Ct, Portland, OR 97203

resources.hoursText: Stops change by date. The next stops are below; this list updates every week from the county calendar.

resources.name: Billi Odegaard Dental Clinic
resources.desc: Dental care: X-rays, cleanings, fillings, and more.
resources.detail: Cost is based on what you can pay. If you can't pay, you can still get care. Suite 380. For severe tooth pain or a broken tooth, call right away.
resources.hoursText: Call to schedule and check hours

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.desc: Free, confidential support for thoughts of suicide, a mental health crisis, or a substance use crisis.
resources.detail: Call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org. Spanish: 1-888-628-9454.

resources.name: Multnomah County Crisis Line
resources.sub: 24/7 mental health crisis line and mobile crisis
resources.desc: Trained clinicians give crisis support, resources, and referrals by phone, for you or someone else. They can also send Project Respond, a crisis team that comes to you.
resources.detail: Free and confidential, any language. Spanish line: 503-988-4853.

resources.name: Cascadia Urgent Walk-In Clinic
resources.desc: Walk in for immediate, in-person help with a mental health or substance use crisis. Free for anyone.

resources.name: Unity Center for Behavioral Health
resources.desc: A 24-hour mental health emergency center. Adults can walk in or be dropped off.
resources.detail: Youth 9-17 need a referral and cannot walk in.

resources.name: Portland Street Response
resources.desc: City teams come in person to help someone having a mental health or behavioral health crisis, anywhere in Portland.
resources.detail: Call 911 or 503-823-7773 and ask for Portland Street Response. A City workers’ strike began Nov 9; the City says critical public safety services continue.

resources.name: YouthLine
resources.sub: Teen-to-teen help line, ages 24 and under
resources.desc: Free support and crisis line for young people. Teens answer 4-10pm; adults answer the phone at other times.
resources.detail: Call, text teen2teen to 839863, or chat at theyouthline.org.

resources.name: The Trevor Project
resources.sub: 24/7 crisis support for LGBTQ+ young people
resources.desc: Free, confidential crisis counseling for LGBTQ+ young people by phone, text, or chat.
resources.detail: Text START to 678-678, or chat at thetrevorproject.org/get-help.

resources.name: Testing 4 All
resources.sub: Cascade AIDS Project: free walk-in HIV testing
resources.desc: Free, confidential HIV testing. Walk in, no appointment.
resources.addr: 520 NW Davis St, Suite 215, Portland, OR 97209

resources.name: Multnomah County STI Clinic
resources.sub: STI and HIV testing and treatment
resources.desc: Testing and treatment for HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia, plus PrEP.
resources.detail: By appointment, no walk-ins. For an urgent need, call to get seen. No ID or insurance needed; no one turned away for inability to pay.

resources.name: Portland Street Medicine
resources.desc: Medical teams who bring care to people sleeping outside or without stable housing. There is no clinic to visit.
resources.detail: Call or text for yourself or someone else. Say where to find the person and what's wrong; the team looks for them on its next rounds. For an emergency, call 911.

resources.name: Wallace Medical Concern
resources.desc: Primary care clinic in East Portland. Treats patients regardless of ability to pay, with a sliding fee based on income.
resources.detail: Appointments only, no walk-ins. Takes OHP. For help signing up for insurance, ask for ext. 4750. Dental care at the same address.

resources.name: Free Naloxone (Narcan)
resources.desc: Naloxone reverses an opioid overdose. Get it free at the county Harm Reduction Clinic, by mail from Just in Case Oregon, or at Outside In (1219 SW Main St).
resources.detail: County Harm Reduction Clinic: 12425 NE Glisan St, in Menlo Park Plaza behind Walgreens, (503) 988-0577. Walk-ins accepted. Also syringe exchange, fentanyl test strips, and testing. Holiday and weather closures: (503) 280-1611. Pharmacies also sell naloxone without a prescription.
resources.hoursText: County clinic Mon & Thu 11am-2pm and 3-7pm. Outside In Mon-Fri noon-5pm. Or call 503-988-3030.

resources.name: Oregon Health Plan (OHP)
resources.desc: Free health coverage for people with low income. Most clinics in this guide take it.
resources.detail: Apply online at ONE.Oregon.gov, by phone, at an ODHS office, or with a free certified helper. You don't need a permanent address; give a phone number, email, or a temporary mailing address.
resources.hoursText: Call ONE Customer Service at 1-800-699-9075, Mon-Fri 7am-6pm

resources.name: Hygiene4All
resources.desc: Free showers under the Morrison Bridge. Soap, towels, hygiene supplies, clean clothing, first aid, and device charging.
resources.addr: SE MLK & Belmont, Portland, OR (under Morrison Bridge)
resources.hoursText: Tue & Thu 3-9pm, Sun 3-7pm. Last shower 45 min before close.

resources.name: The Wash House
resources.desc: Free laundry service. Drop off one bag (up to 40 lbs), pick up same day or next day.

resources.name: 13 Salmon Shower Project
resources.desc: Free showers and clean clothing, open to anyone who wants a shower. First come, first served.
resources.detail: You don't need to belong to the church. ADA accessible. Lower level of the Buchan building at SW 13th & Salmon.

resources.name: NW Glisan Oasis Day Center
resources.sub: City day center: showers, laundry, charging
resources.desc: An open-air City day center with showers, washers and dryers, a clothing closet, phone charging, and a place to warm up or cool down.
resources.detail: Anyone can use it. First aid, transit help, and bike repair. A mobile health clinic comes Fridays 10am-5pm. Run by Urban Alchemy. The City warns budget cuts may change City-funded sites.

resources.name: City Day Storage
resources.desc: Store your things safely for the day, overnight, or up to 30 days. Free.
resources.detail: Everything must fit in a 32-gallon bin with the lid closed. No carts, weapons, food, or liquids. Items left 30 days are thrown away; daily check-in preferred. First come, first served.

resources.name: Ground Score Storage
resources.desc: Locked daytime storage for up to 3 containers, with free coffee, snacks, and phone charging.
resources.detail: New members sign a short agreement. Email hello@groundscoreassociation.org.

resources.name: Marie Equi Center
resources.desc: A day center for LGBTQIA2S+ people, especially low-income and unhoused: peer support, mail, computers, harm reduction, and help with housing and benefits.
resources.detail: Hours are from the County day center list; call to confirm.

resources.name: PAW Team
resources.sub: Free vet care and pet food
resources.desc: Free vet care for pets of people experiencing homelessness, and a Pet Food and Supply Bank.
resources.detail: Vet clinic by appointment: fill out the pre-screening form on the website first. No emergency care. Pet Supply Bank once a month.

resources.name: Multnomah County Central Library
resources.desc: Free computers (4 hours a day), Wi-Fi, and up to 100 pages of free printing a day, plus free copying, fax and scanning. Restrooms, warmth, quiet space.
resources.detail: No library card needed to print. No card for computers? Ask at the desk for a daily guest pass with photo ID, or just your name and birthdate. Wi-Fi here works only while the library is open. 13 more library branches across Portland offer the same free services.
resources.hoursText: Call 503-988-5123 or check multcolib.org for today's hours. Closed Dec 24, Dec 25 and Jan 1.

resources.name: Albina Library
resources.sub: Multnomah County Library: free computers + Wi-Fi
resources.desc: Free Wi-Fi, computers (4 hours a day), and up to 100 pages of free printing a day, plus free copying, fax and scanning. Restrooms inside.
resources.detail: No library card needed to print. No card for computers? Ask at the desk for a daily guest pass with photo ID, or just your name and birthdate. Wi-Fi "Library_WiFi" (no password) works 5am to midnight, even outside after closing. Outlets are limited, so come charged.
resources.hoursText: Call 503-988-5123 or check multcolib.org for today's hours. Closed Dec 24, Dec 25 and Jan 1.

resources.name: Court Legal Resource Center
resources.sub: Free help if you go to court without a lawyer
resources.desc: Free help with court forms and procedures for family, landlord-tenant, and small claims cases.
resources.detail: Free for anyone without a lawyer. Staff explain procedures but cannot give legal advice. A limited number of walk-in spots each day.

resources.name: Multnomah Project Reset
resources.sub: Get Multnomah County fines and fees forgiven
resources.desc: Each month 60 people with low incomes are picked at random to have their Multnomah County court fines and fees waived. No community service needed.
resources.detail: Sign up online; if not picked, you stay in the pool for next month. Run by Metropolitan Public Defender with the court and DA.
resources.hoursText: Sign up online, or call and leave a message

resources.name: CLEAR Clinic
resources.sub: Free criminal and eviction record clearing
resources.desc: Free legal help to clear criminal records and eviction records, plus some immigration help.
resources.detail: Walk-in clinics at locations around Portland; see the drop-in calendar on the website. No appointment needed at drop-ins.
resources.addr: 537 SE Ash St, Suite 202, Portland, OR 97214
resources.hoursText: See the drop-in calendar on the website

resources.name: Legal Aid Services of Oregon
resources.sub: Free civil legal help, Portland office
resources.desc: Free legal help for low-income people with public benefits, tenant and housing problems, and family law and protection orders.
resources.detail: Intake is by phone. Interpreters available. Toll-free 1-800-228-6958.

resources.name: Eviction Defense Project
resources.sub: Oregon Law Center: free help facing eviction
resources.desc: Free legal help for low-income tenants with an eviction court case.
resources.detail: Contact them at least 48 business hours before your first court date. Have your case number and hearing date ready. In Multnomah County, help may start as soon as you get a termination notice.
resources.hoursText: Call or use the web form

resources.name: TriMet Reduced Fare
resources.desc: If you receive OHP (Medicaid), SNAP, or TANF, you qualify for $1.25 fare (normally $2.50). Hop Fastpass daily cap: $5.
resources.detail: Age 65+ or Medicare/disability = $1.00 fare. Trip planner: trimet.org/tripplanner
resources.hoursText: Apply at trimet.org/reducedfare, or call (503) 238-7433 Mon-Fri 8am-4pm

resources.name: Honest Day
resources.sub: Free recovery app from Healing Nations Foundation
resources.desc: A guided 120-day recovery practice on your phone: a daily check-in, short lessons, a journal, and a toolkit for cravings and hard nights. Crisis help is one tap away.
resources.detail: Free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, with no ads. Android is coming soon. Your journal never leaves your phone.
resources.highlight: Free. Try it whenever you are ready.

resources.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
resources.desc: Free, confidential help finding local treatment, support groups, and recovery services. English and Spanish.

resources.name: VA Community Resource and Referral Center
resources.desc: Walk-in center for veterans and their families who are homeless or at risk: housing, health care, and benefits help in one place.
resources.detail: Moved in September 2026 from SW 1st Ave. No emergency services on site.
resources.hoursText: Walk in Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri 8am-2:30pm; Thu 10am-2:30pm

resources.name: VA Portland
resources.desc: Healthcare, mental health, housing programs, and employment assistance for eligible veterans.
resources.addr: 3710 SW U.S. Veterans Hospital Rd, Portland, OR

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line
resources.desc: Dial 988, then press 1. Available 24/7. You can also text 838255.
resources.highlight: If you're in crisis, call now. You are not alone.
